PullRequest.Title: Underline chat carousel links in high-contrast themes
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #334647

## Summary

Restore a consistent link cue in high-contrast chat question carousels. The global HC rule only underlines direct `p > a` links, so anchors nested inside bold text, emphasis, headings, and lists miss it.

- Add a carousel-scoped underline rule for both high-contrast themes, without changing global link styling or theme colors.
- Add eight real-widget regression cases covering four theme classes with the underline-links preference on and off. Each checks plain, bold, italic, heading, and list links in the carousel message, question title, and detailed content.
- Expand the existing MarkdownLinks fixture and add opt-in light high-contrast support using the built-in theme resource and the existing fixture helpers.

Link activation and keyboard handling are unchanged. The hover-color question in #334651 remains separate.

## Validation

- **81 targeted tests passed**:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatQuestionCarouselPart.test.ts
```

- Before the fix, all four HC regression cases failed while all four normal-theme cases passed. All eight new regressions passed again with the final scoped selector.
- Verified the real-widget fixture in dark, light, dark high contrast, and light high contrast. All six visible links are underlined in each HC theme, with unchanged link colors.
- Normal dark/light before-and-after screenshots are byte-for-byte identical.
- Focused title links retain an underline and visible focus outline; hovered title links retain the underline and existing active-link color token.
- ESLint, diff checks, and pre-commit hygiene passed. Stylelint passed with four pre-existing design-token suggestions; existing CSS diagnostics were left untouched.
- The automated fixture-error scan was unavailable because the Component Explorer daemon browser was closed. Rendering, style measurements, and screenshots were validated through the integrated browser instead.

## Manual verification

Open the `chat/chatQuestionCarousel/MarkdownLinks` fixture in DarkHighContrast and LightHighContrast. Confirm that links in the introduction, bold question title, detailed heading, paragraph, and list are underlined at rest. Focus and hover the title link, then switch to Dark and Light to confirm their existing styling is preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or navigate a chat question carousel in a dark or light high-contrast workbench
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Carousel Markdown rendering creates the currently visible message/title/details DOM, after which browser style resolution matches the added high-contrast rule. No asynchronous operation or external boundary must complete for the underline rule itself.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The added selector is evaluated for anchors in rendered Markdown; cost grows with the number of visible carousel Markdown links, not with question history or all workspace content. Navigation renders one current question at a time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous browser style matching on the UI thread; no queue, IPC, subprocess, or concurrent fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved. Browser stylesheet/selector machinery is reused normally; theme changes may trigger style recalculation as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed CSS and carousel render path: the diff adds only text-decoration declarations and no geometry reads, DOM reconstruction, event loop, or expensive boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact selector-match timing depends on DOM size, but the two simple, scoped selectors add constant rule count and only match visible anchors, so no meaningful regression mechanism is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The rule adds bounded selector matching and paint styling without forced layout, repeated JavaScript work, retained state, or external calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the ChatQuestionCarouselPart browser unit suite
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each of eight new fixed test cases renders one widget and synchronously reads computed text decoration for three groups of five links; these reads are test-only and complete before each assertion.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed at 8 cases and 15 computed-style reads per case (120 reads total), independent of user data or repository size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial synchronous test execution; no Promise fan-out or boundary concurrency is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The production stylesheet is imported once by the test module. Each test creates a bounded DOM root, and teardown removes widget DOM while the suite disposable store owns added cleanup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the generated test loops and computed-style map calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runner-specific style calculation duration is unmeasured, but cardinality is small and fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The extra work is deliberate, bounded regression coverage and does not affect product runtime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and capture the MarkdownLinks component fixture across normal and high-contrast themes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selected fixture awaits theme setup, renders one carousel, and the screenshot harness captures the variant. Adding two high-contrast variants increases this fixture's coverage from two theme renders to four when all variants are captured.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture and compare a rendered component screenshot for each blocking fixture variant
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four fixed theme variants after the diff versus two non-blocking normal-theme variants before; two variants are newly defined for this fixture, while making it blocksCi places all four in blocking screenshot coverage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The MarkdownLinks fixture had only Dark and Light variants and was not labeled blocksCi.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each selected CI fixture variant must render before its screenshot can be captured; this affects test infrastructure only.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed per-fixture theme count: Dark, Light, DarkHighContrast, and LightHighContrast. It does not scale with workspace, chat history, or user content.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The fixture framework notes explorer UI fixtures may render in parallel; screenshot/CI scheduling is external to this changed code. Within a render, theme and file-icon-theme loading use Promise.all.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Theme loads are coalesced per ColorThemeData in a WeakMap. The light high-contrast JSON is statically bundled; its resource lookup is in-memory, and actual theme loading occurs on first use with warm renders sharing the promise. No network or filesystem read is introduced for this theme.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in variant cardinality, cached theme loading, and absence of network/filesystem reads from the inspected fixture framework; screenshot process scheduling remains external.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The external screenshot runner's parallelism and exact capture duration are not shown, but the increase is a fixed two variants plus bounded blocking coverage rather than input-dependent fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The fixed CI/test cost is intentional regression coverage, and the added theme resource does not introduce unbounded work or a product-path performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load the component-fixture bundle and first use the light high-contrast theme
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The fixture utility module includes one additional built-in theme source and constructs lightweight ColorThemeData metadata eagerly; JSONC theme processing is deferred until setupTheme first requests that theme.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional built-in theme resource of fixed size; actual loading is once per theme object and then cached.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: On first fixture render, color-theme and file-icon-theme setup run concurrently via Promise.all; duplicate color-theme requests share one cached promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold light-high-contrast use invokes ensureLoaded once through the in-memory extension resource loader. Warm uses reuse themeLoadedPromises. The changed theme path resolves from themeJsonModules, so the fallback fetch path is not reached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from static imports, the in-memory map, setupTheme, and WeakMap promise cache.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The precise bundle-byte and parse-time increase is not measured, but it is one bounded test-only resource and does not grow over fixture lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. There is small fixed test-tool bundle overhead, but no realistic scaling or critical product impact meeting the reporting threshold.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete five-file diff and traced production carousel rendering, unit-test computed-style checks, component screenshot variants, and built-in theme initialization. No actionable performance regression was introduced; no findings or regression-fix records were submitted.
